As in previous years, Apple is expected to launch the iPhone 18 series this fall as usual in September, though this year's event will echo several aspects of the special circumstances surrounding the iPhone launch during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic.

Ways this fall's iPhone event may differ from Apple's usual approach

Apple has many highly successful products, but the iPhone remains its flagship and accounts for a large share of the company's overall revenue.

So it makes sense that Apple works hard to maintain consistency around its iPhone launches. By keeping a stable schedule for new iPhone releases, it can better meet the expectations of Wall Street and consumers.

Typically, Apple unveils new iPhones in early September—usually four new models—with all of them going on sale by late September.

But 2020 was an exception due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

That fall's iPhone lineup wasn't announced until October, and only two of the new models went on sale initially, with the other two arriving in November.

This year, rumors suggest Apple may face similar variables in its launch plans.

While a September event remains the broad expectation, Apple may not put all new iPhone models on sale at the same time.

As in 2020, only two models may be available for purchase initially: the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The much-anticipated foldable iPhone Ultra is expected to be unveiled in September, but rumors suggest its release date may be slightly delayed, possibly arriving several weeks after the Pro models go on sale.

Apple may also deviate from its usual approach in terms of the total number of iPhone models.

If rumors that the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 will be pushed back to spring 2027 prove accurate, only three new models will debut this fall—making it the smallest fall iPhone lineup since 2019.

Whether driven by strategic considerations or by challenges such as the global memory chip shortage and the complexities of mass-producing an entirely new foldable device, Apple's fall 2026 event may reprise several elements of 2020.

What are you most hoping to see at this fall's iPhone event? Let us know in the comments.
